craft_notes: Sthāyin: exhausted-rites (tired tongue, tired mind). Rows: row 1 (tired→name?). Close: name (nāma as landing: what NAME). Rejected: 'prayer' for meditation — kept meditation (dhyāna precise); 'God' for formless — kept formless (arūpa as the rite's object).

lines: Tongue weary of your name, mind weary of your recall.
Formless one — what meditation? Qualityless — what name?
l4.sanskrit_cite: jihvā śrāntā bhavannāmni manaḥ śrāntaṃ bhavatsmṛtau | arūpasya kuto dhyāna nirguṇasya ca nāma kim

reads_against.argmap: What use are rites for the formless? → Rites exhausted at the start: tired tongue, tired mind — meditation with no form to hold, name with no quality to name.
c1_essence: Rites exhausted at the start: tired tongue, tired mind — meditation with no form, name with no quality.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta settling into established holding (stillness that stays)
